title: Self-Driving Cars & Autonomous Systems
tagline: Follow the self-driving stack from sensors and localization through perception, prediction, and planning to end-to-end models and simulation.
prereqs: Deep Learning and Computer Vision. Robotics & Embodied AI helps for the planning and imitation steps.

steps.title: Introduction to self-driving
steps.why: Waabi's overview of the problem and the classic autonomy stack.

steps.title: Sensors and hardware
steps.why: Cameras, lidar, radar, and compute, and what each sees.

steps.title: Kalman filters
steps.why: Fuse noisy measurements with a motion model to track state.

steps.title: Localization
steps.why: Work out where the car is on the map, to centimeters.

steps.title: HD maps
steps.why: What goes into driving maps and how they are built.

steps.title: Perception
steps.why: Detect and track cars and pedestrians in 3D from sensor data.

steps.title: Bird's-eye-view 3D perception
steps.why: MIT talk on efficient 3D perception, including camera and lidar BEV fusion.

steps.title: Motion forecasting
steps.why: Predict where other road users will move next.

steps.title: Motion planning and control
steps.why: Choose a safe trajectory, then follow it with steering and throttle.

steps.title: Imitation learning for driving
steps.why: Tübingen lecture on learning to drive from human demonstrations.

steps.title: End-to-end driving
steps.why: Wayve's CEO on replacing the hand-built stack with one learned model.

steps.title: Simulation
steps.why: Test driving software in simulated worlds before it reaches the road.

steps.title: How openpilot controls a real car
steps.why: comma's engineer on sending steering and speed commands to stock cars.

projects: Implement a 1D and then 2D Kalman filter that tracks a simulated car from noisy GPS readings.
Drive a car along waypoints in the CARLA simulator with a PID controller and plot the tracking error.
Train a small behavior-cloning model in CARLA or a 2D driving sim and report how often it leaves the lane.
